description: Runs a program written in a BASIC-like language, reading nine input jacks, driving six output jacks and printing Tipsy text; the program is typed into the window on the panel

params.text: Pressing it starts the program under the two trigger styles of STYLE, and under the gate style the program runs for as long as the button is held down
Chooses when the program runs: always, start on a trigger and loop back to the top, start on a trigger and stop at the last line, or run while a gate is high

inputs.text: Carries a voltage the program reads under its own printed name, IN1 through IN9; a polyphonic cable makes its channels readable as an array
A trigger starts the program under the two trigger styles of STYLE; under the gate style the program runs while this is high and picks up where it stopped when it goes high again

outputs.text: Carries the value the program assigns to its own printed name, OUT1 through OUT6, clamped to -10V to 10V unless the menu unclamps that one

notes: nothing runs until a program is typed into the code window; while that window is empty the lit word on the panel reads Fix
nineteen worked programs ship with the module, under Preset in its right-click menu
the lit word on the panel reads Good when the program has compiled and Fix when it has not, and hovering over Fix describes the first error found
right-clicking the code window gives Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all; the module's own menu is on the panel around that window
menu: Title above IN1-3 — a text field for a short name printed above the input jacks, which helps when several of these are in a patch
Screen Colors — picks the ink and paper of the code window from seven pairs
Font — picks the typeface of the code window, from VCV font (like Notes), four RobotoMono weights and three RobotoSlab weights
Highlight error line — marks the line the compiler stopped at; unset, no line is marked
Colorblind-friendly status light — changes the Good and Fix light from green and red to blue and orange, and the error mark to orange
Clamp OUTn values to (-10V, 10V) — a submenu holding OUT1 to OUT6, each of which either keeps that output inside -10V to 10V or lets it carry the true value of the variable
Syntax — a submenu of the statements of the language; choosing one inserts it into the code
Math — a submenu of the built-in functions, each with a one-line description; choosing one inserts a call to it into the code
Text — a submenu of the string variables and the print and debug functions; choosing one inserts it into the code
